paper_title: Valid Per-Field Selective Risk Control for Document Extraction: Three Failure Modes, a Validity Ladder, and When Conditioning Pays

sections.title: Abstract
sections.content: Per-field accept/review with selective risk at most alpha -- accept a field only if the error rate among accepted fields is controlled -- is the trust contract document-extraction systems need, and the natural procedure silently violates it on real documents. On 13,859 genuine claude-sonnet-5 fields from 800 CORD receipts (49.0% correct) we diagnose three failure modes: document clustering (design effect 1.84-2.45), score-refit leakage (coverage 0.416 at risk 0.127, violating alpha=0.10 in 95% of splits), and a tie-mass pathology (a degenerate score collapses the threshold grid, 0.030 to 0.001). We organize the fixes as a validity ladder, guarantee form stated per tier. A fit/val split protocol restores expected-selective-risk control for a learned fusion: coverage 0.318 at risk 0.096 at nominal alpha=0.10, no tolerance band (production variant 0.326) -- an on-average point whose realized risk exceeds alpha in 47.5% of resplits, not a certificate. Mondrian Learn-then-Test with exact binomial tails yields per-group PAC certificates: field-iid 0.171 at risk 0.068, cluster-corrected 0.140, doc-iid 0.060 -- the only tier matching documents, honestly near-vacuous today. Support-bin, the pre-specified provenance taxonomy, wins every rigor tier on the sonnet CORD capture (p<1e-4, Bonferroni-corrected) -- a win that does not replicate on the same documents under haiku or qwen -- while on higher-accuracy corpora pooled thresholds win: conditioning helps exactly where pooled cannot certify, subsumed by a learned score elsewhere. A frozen-configuration confirmation on selection-untouched claude-haiku-4-5 held at both risk levels, and a blind three-annotator human-gold audit verifies the practical tier's accepted-set risk at 1.3% against its 10% budget (Fleiss' kappa=0.83; labels err one-sidedly pessimistic). Released Apache-2.0 with seed-pinned, regression-gated procedures.

sections.title: Abstract
sections.content: Per-field accept/review with selective risk at most α accept field only if the error rate among accepted fields is controlled is the trust contract document-extraction systems need, and the natural procedure (threshold confidence score via an add-one bound on calibration split) silently violates it on real documents. On 13,859 genuine claude-sonnet-5 fields from 800 CORD receipts (49.0% field correctness) we diagnose and quantify three failure modes: document clustering (a design effect of 1.842.45 that roughly halves the effective calibration size), score-refit leakage (fitting learned score and its threshold on the same fields: coverage 0.416 at risk 0.127, violating nominal α=0.10 in 95% of splits), and tie-mass pathology (a degenerate score distribution collapses the threshold grid; counterfactual zeroing of single signal reproduces 0.030 0.001 collapse of certified coverage). We organize the fixes as validity ladder with the guarantee form stated per tier. fit/val split protocol restores expected-selective-risk control for learned fusion score: coverage 0.318 at achieved risk 0.096 at nominal α=0.10 with no tolerance band (production variant 0.326 at 0.097) an on-average operating point whose realized risk exceeds α in 47.5% of resplits, not certificate. Mondrian Learn-then-Test with exact binomial tails yields per-group PAC certificates: field-iid 0.171 coverage at risk 0.068 (violations 0.03), cluster-corrected 0.140 at 0.051, and doc-iid 0.060 at 0.020 the only tier whose assumptions match documents, and honestly near-vacuous today. Support-bin, the pre-specified grounding-derived provenance taxonomy, wins every rigor tier on the sonnet CORD capture (p < 104, sign-flip over 40 document-level resplits; Bonferroni-corrected over taxonomies) win that does not replicate on the same documents under haiku or qwen (7) while on higher-accuracy corpora pooled thresholds win: conditioning rescues certification exactly where pooled threshold cannot certify, and learned score subsumes it elsewhere. frozen-configuration confirmation on selection-untouched claude-haiku-4-5 capture held at both risk levels (0.167 at 0.093; 0.068 at 0.037), and blind three-annotator human-gold audit verifies the practical tiers accepted-set risk at 1.3% against its 10% budget (Fleiss κ=0.83; automatic calibration labels err one-sidedly pessimistic). Released Apache-2.0 with seed-pinned, regression-gated procedures.

sections.title: 1 Introduction
sections.content: Document parsers now read pages fluently and still emit silently-wrong structured values (Ferguson et al., 2026). The remedy the field converges on is per-field trust contract: each extracted field carries confidence and an accept/review decision, and the system promises that the selective risk the error rate among accepted fields stays below target α. The natural implementation is folklore: fit confidence score, hold out calibration split, and pick the smallest threshold whose add-one-smoothed empirical selective risk is α (Geifman & El-Yaniv, 2019; Angelopoulos et al., 2024). This paper shows, on genuine frontier-LLM 1 output at scale, that the folklore procedure silently violates the contract on real documents and shows what to run instead, at three explicit levels of rigor. Our testbed is deliberately hard and deliberately real: 13,859 per-field predictions captured from claude-sonnet-5 on 800 CORD receipts, of which only 49.0% are correct, plus FUNSD and XFUNDde captures spanning the difficulty spectrum  (Table 1)  ; construction, labels, and measurement findings are in the companion benchmark paper (Gurram, 2026).1 (C1) Diagnosis. Three quantified failure modes of naive per-field selective guarantees Contributions. on documents document clustering (design effect 1.842.45), score-refit leakage (risk 0.127 at nominal 0.10, 95% of splits violating), and tie-mass pathology (a degenerate score collapses the threshold grid) each pinned by counterfactual experiment (4). None had been quantified for document extraction. (C2) Protocol. validity ladder as reporting standard (5): practical tier (fit/val split protocol + add-one; controls expected selective risk), rigorous field-iid PAC tier (Mondrian Learn-then-Test with exact binomial tails, per-group (risk > α) δ), and rigorous doc-iid PAC tier (per-document bound; the exchangeability unit that matches documents), each row annotated with its estimand, assumption, and violation fraction. (C3) Result. The first held-at-nominal operating points and PAC certificates on genuine frontier-LLM extraction at scale (6), with provenance (grounding-derived support bins) the pre-specified conditioning taxonomy that wins every rigor tier on the hard regimes sonnet capture (p < 104) model-scoped result, not corpus-general one: 7 shows the same win collapses on the identical documents under weaker-signal model. (C4) Characterization. two-regime empirical law with stated mechanism (7): with learned accept score, covariates belong in the score (Mondrian conditioning is subsumed and can hurt); with frozen or weak score, they belong in the taxonomy and taxonomy-side conditioning pays exactly where the pooled threshold cannot certify at the target α. (C5) Artifact. An open, decoupled harness: 40 fixed document-level splits (seed 7), bit-exact sanity gates chained across experiments, 463/624-cells-bit-identical regression check, and full disclosure of capture-stage data defect and its forensics (Appendix B). We claim no new conformal theory: the machinery is classical (Vovk et al., 2003; Angelopoulos et al., 2021; 2024). The contributions are the diagnoses, the protocol, the certified application, and the characterization.

sections.title: 2 Related Work
sections.content: Confidence for extraction. Beyond Logprobs (Preprint authors, 2026a) fuses logprobs and consistency for document field confidence with ECE/AUROC/selective-risk reporting; Cleanlab TLM (Cleanlab, 2025) sells model-agnostic per-field trust scores; real-time trustworthiness scoring (Preprint authors, 2026d) is similar. None attaches grounding, and none provides risk-controlled accept/review guarantee the axes added here and in the companion benchmark (Gurram, 2026). Grounding for KIE is itself established (DocILEs KILE task (Šimša et al., 2023), SROIE (Huang et al., 2019), OCRBench v2 (Fu et al., 2025), BoundingDocs (Preprint authors, 2025a)); we use provenance as conditioning covariate for risk control, not as an output format. Uncertainty signals such as semantic entropy (Farquhar et al., 2024) and consistency/verbalized fusion (Chen & Mueller, 2023) share blind spot (self-consistent errors), motivating the external verification signal grounding support our taxonomy uses. Selective prediction and risk control. The add-one selective-risk threshold is the selective-classification bound of Geifman & El-Yaniv (2019); conformal risk control (Angelopoulos et al., 2024), conformal factuality (Mohri & Hashimoto, 2024), and selective CRC (Preprint authors, 2025b) control marginal risk. Learn-then-Test (Angelopoulos et al., 2021) converts risk control into multiple testing our rigorous tiers instantiate it with exact binomial tails (Clopper & Pearson, 1934) and Holm step-down (Holm, 1979). Conditional-coverage theory (Gibbs et al., 2025) shows exact per-instance conditioning is impossible while exact group-conditional control is attainable (Mondrian CP (Vovk et al., 2003)); risk-controlling prediction sets (Bates et al., 2021) give the PAC form we state. CRC-certify (Preprint authors, 2026b) defines fieldlevel JSON losses and abstention bounds but does not condition on provenance and does not diagnose the 1Companion papers: this paper owns the procedures, guarantees, diagnoses, and characterization; VerifyDocBench (Gurram, 2026) owns the datasets, labeling protocol and reliability audit, and the model/language measurement study. Numbers here are reproducible from the released harness (seed-pinned splits, regression-gated procedures). 2 document-specific failure modes that are this papers subject. Risk-controlled generative OCR (Preprint authors, 2026c) and VISA (Preprint authors, 2024) establish visual attribution; Traub & Kirchhof (2024) the evaluation side of selective prediction.

sections.title: 3 Setup
sections.content: 3.1 Task and trust contract Given document and JSON schema S, an extractor outputs leaf fields with values; trust layer attaches to each field confidence [0, 1], grounding (page/bbox/char-span with support score), and decision in {accept, review}. The contract: maximize coverage (fraction accepted) subject to selective risk (error rate among accepted) α. Correctness labels are schema-typed (exact/numeric/semantic per leaf); omission and hallucination are scored separately (Gurram, 2026). 3.2 Data: genuine frontier-LLM captures All headline experiments run on genuine per-field output of claude-sonnet-5 (k=3 self-consistency), captured once and frozen  (Table 1)  . These captures are text-layer prompted: the model reads the documents OCR text layer, not the page image despite VLM being the natural shorthand for closed frontier API model, no vision capability is exercised anywhere in this papers headline results (the companion benchmark papers cross-vendor gpt-4o row is the one genuinely vision-based capture in either paper; see (Gurram, 2026)). CORD is the hard regime: only 49.0% of asserted fields are correct, yet grounding is strongly discriminative (grounded-vs-ungrounded correctness gap +0.352, 95% document-clustered CI [0.33, 0.37]; verbalized AUROC 0.845 [0.83, 0.86]) (Gurram, 2026). The claude-haiku-4-5 capture is reserved for the frozen-configuration confirmation (6.4) and touched by no selection step. Table 1: Genuine per-field captures used in this paper. correct = fraction of asserted fields scored correct; grounded = fraction with located source. The haiku capture is selection-untouched (confirmation only). dump extractor fields docs correct grounded CORD FUNSD XFUND-de CORD (confirmation) claude-sonnet-5 claude-sonnet-5 claude-sonnet-5 claude-haiku-4-5 13,859 1,999 523 5,341 800 175 42 400 0.490 0.676 0.771 0.567 0.607 0.825 0.774 0.708 3.3 Signals and accept scores Per field we compute five signals: verbalized self-report, k-sample self-consistency, grounded flag, an entailment-NLI score of the value against its source region, and ambiguity-penalized grounding support. Support is the trust-relevant provenance signal: when predicted value matches equally-good page locations (a bare 2 matches many tokens), we retain support = score/m. Under uniform prior over the equally-good matches with exactly one true source, 1/m is the chance given match is the source well-behaved heuristic (not claim of optimality) that quarantines coincidental short-value matches out of the well-grounded group. Table 2 ablates the penalty form; softer forms (1/ m, 1/(1+ ln m)) under-penalize and leave coincidental matches (and their error) in the grounded group. Two accept scores are used throughout. The shared low-capacity fusion is 5-signal logistic regression (the black-box default; we do not call it fixed because it is refit per split see the caveat in 6.1). The learned fusion (hgb_split) is depth-3 histogram gradient-boosted tree over the five signals plus engineered features (value length, digit fraction, is-numeric, signal interactions, and field-type one-hots), with document-level early stopping; test AUROC on CORD 0.925 vs 0.871 for the LR. _noent variants drop the NLI signal. 3 Table 2: Ablation of the ambiguity-penalty form: support retained for unit-score match found at equally-good locations. The uniform-prior 1/m demotes ambiguous matches most aggressively; softer forms under-penalize. matches none 1/ 1/(1+ ln m) 1/m (ours) 1 2 4 1.00 1.00 1.00 1.00 1.00 0.71 0.50 0.35 1.00 0.59 0.42 0.32 1.00 0.50 0.25 0.125 3.4 Conditioning taxonomies Mondrian conditioning applies the identical threshold rule within each group of taxonomy (Vovk et al., 2003). Candidates: pooled (one group); support-bin (terciles of ambiguity-penalized support at calibration quantiles 0.34/0.67) the pre-specified provenance taxonomy, declared as this projects thesis in pre-campaign drafts before any scale experiment ran; fieldtype-freq (leaf-key vocabulary, keys with 25 calibration fields); fieldtype-rule (fixed keyword map, data-independent). All data-dependent taxonomy parts (bin edges, vocabularies) are computed from threshold-fitting rows only. 3.5 Evaluation protocol: what held means Every number is mean over 40 fixed document-level 50/50 calibration/test splits (numpy generator seed 7; fields of one document never straddle split), at nominal α with no tolerance band. configuration is held iff its mean achieved test selective risk is α; we always co-report the coverage standard deviation across splits and viol, the fraction of splits whose realized risk exceeds α. Paired differences use two-sided sign-flip permutation tests (20,000 flips): their floor is 1/20,001, so we write < 104, never smaller; because the 40 resplits share documents, these p-values measure split-resampling stability on this corpus, not population-level significance. Zero-coverage splits contribute risk 0 (disclosed wherever it matters, 6.1).

sections.title: 4 Why naive per-field selective guarantees fail on documents
sections.content: The add-one rule picks the smallest threshold τ whose smoothed empirical selective risk on calibration is α: τ = min : 1+#{i: cit, erri} 1+#{i: cit} α , τ = (review everything) if none qualifies. Under exchangeability of calibration and test fields this controls the expected selective risk at α (Geifman & El-Yaniv, 2019; Angelopoulos et al., 2024; Preprint authors, 2025b). On real documents, three separate mechanisms break it  (Table 3)  . The before exhibit is the operating point an earlier draft of this work headlined: coverage 0.114 at achieved risk 0.122 (78% of splits violating) at nominal α=0.10 produced by exactly these mechanisms plus taxonomy selection. Table 3: Three diagnosed failure modes, each pinned by counterfactual. All at nominal α=0.10, 40 document-level splits. failure mode counterfactual evidence magnitude document clustering score-refit leakage clean-fit control (score fit on held-out docs) still overshoots: risk 0.105, 50% of splits same-half vs split-half fit of the identical learned score tie-mass pathology zeroing one signal on the intact dump reproduces the collapse design effect 1.842.45; pooled add-one risk 0.1030.106 on all three corpora; grouped variant 0.122 at 78% of splits same-half: coverage 0.416 at risk 0.127, 95% of splits violate; split protocol: 0.266 at 0.092 1,702257 distinct scores; certified coverage 0.0300.001; doc-level add-one 0.0370.000 4 Failure 1: document clustering invalidates the marginal bound. Fields cluster within documents, and calibration/test splits are (and must be) document-level. At the add-one threshold the estimated design effect is 2.15 (CORD), 1.84 (FUNSD), 2.04 (XFUND-de) up to 2.45 at other thresholds so the effective calibration sample is roughly half its nominal size. On the 6,901-field CORD dump the pooled add-one rule lands at achieved risk 0.105, violating in 50% of splits (FUNSD and XFUND-de likewise, Table 3). The mean overshoot is hair clusterings main effect is per-split variance but the many-group groundedsupport taxonomy shows the badly-broken case: risk 0.122 with 78% of splits violating. clean-fit control (score fit on held-out documents, threshold on the rest) still overshoots (0.105, 50%), isolating clustering from refit leakage. Failure 2: score-refit leakage. Fitting high-capacity score and its threshold on the same calibration fields transfers the scores optimism into the threshold. The depth-3 gradient-boosted fusion under the same-half protocol posts coverage 0.416 at risk 0.127, violating in 95% of splits an invalid operating point that looks spectacular. 5-parameter logistic fusion barely overfits (risk 0.105), which is why the flaw goes unnoticed until score capacity grows. The fix is protocol, not prose (5.1). Failure 3: tie-mass pathology (discrete scores break threshold grids). Our first 13,859-field capture silently shipped an all-zero entailment column (the NLI stage was skipped mid-capture; Appendix B). With only coarse discrete signals left, the fused score collapsed from 1,702 distinct calibration values (intact 6.9k dump) to 257, with tie masses of 221 and 183 fields at the acceptance head. threshold accepts tie mass whole or not at all: the smallest reachable candidate accepted n=245 fields at empirical risk 0.114 > α, so no certificate existed at any confidence level rigorous certified coverage collapsed 0.030 0.001 and the doc-level add-one to exactly 0. Causality is pinned counterfactually: zeroing entailment on the intact dump reproduces the collapse (0.0302 0.0011), and nothing else changed. Two harness lessons generalize to any discrete or heavily-tied score: (i) snap candidate thresholds to distinct-value boundaries (label-independent, hence free of validity cost; regression-gated 463/624 cells bit-identical, max headline drift 0.0088, and the grid fix alone moves certified coverage by 0.004, i.e. the pathology was the score, not the grid); (ii) argsort-based diagnostics silently cherry-pick inside tie masses the threshold-realizable top-1% error was 0.071 vs the argsort illusion of 0.046.

sections.title: 5 Procedures: a validity ladder
sections.content: 5.1 Tier 12 fix: the fit/val split protocol Split the calibration half (by document) into fit half and val half. Fit the score model and every data-dependent transform (vocabularies, standardization, early stopping) on the fit half only; compute the add-one threshold and all Mondrian bin edges on the untouched val half; never touch test. This restores scorethreshold independence it does not restore exchangeability, so document clustering remains and tiers 12 stay marginal, on-average guarantees. On the 6.9k CORD dump the same learned score moves from an invalid 0.416/0.127 (95% violating) to 0.266 at 0.092 (held). Residual disclosure: support-bin edges and fieldtype vocabularies are computed on the same val half as the threshold; both are label-independent and second-order. 5.2 Tier 34 fix: Mondrian Learn-then-Test with exact binomial tails For each taxonomy group and candidate threshold t, we test H0 : selective risk of in > α with an exact binomial tail p-value (Clopper & Pearson, 1934) on the calibration errors among accepted fields, then select thresholds by family-wise-error-controlled multiple testing (Angelopoulos et al., 2021): half the budget δ to Holm step-down (Holm, 1979), half to fixed-sequence pass from the most conservative candidate (the mix rule; union bound keeps it valid at δ, and it is the only variant that never collapses across our three corpora). Candidates are 15 geometric acceptance-fraction quantiles (1%100%) of the groups calibration scores, snapped to the nearest distinct-value boundary label-independent, so multiplicity is paid only over 15 points; naive fine grid destroys certification (pooled certified coverage 0.0009 vs 0.0055 on the 6.9k dump). Budgets: per-group (δ per group, three separate statements) or simultaneous (δ/G). Guarantee (tier 5 3, per group): with probability 1 δ over the calibration draw, the true selective risk among accepted fields in that group is α, if within-group accepted-field errors are iid. The iid premise is load-bearing, not decorative: the measured design effect 2 means the binomial overstates evidence about twofold; we therefore co-report cluster-corrected variant (ltt.neff: binomial deflated by the plug-in design effect) at every headline. Guarantee (tier 4): replace the field unit by the document with probability 1 δ, the mean per-document error rate among accepting documents is α (finite-sample bound, documents iid). Tier 4 is the only tier whose assumptions match the data-generating process; note it bounds macro per-document functional, not field-level (micro) selective risk. Disclosure (score refit). As implemented, tiers 24 refit the 5-signal LR on the calibration half on which the LTT p-values are computed formally the same premise violation as Failure 2. The clean-fit control bounds the effect at 0 for this 5-parameter score, and the split-protocol twin of tier 2 (0.212 vs 0.218, 6.1) confirms it empirically; running tiers 34 on the frozen fit-half score is protocol hygiene we adopt for the camera-ready harness. 5.3 Taxonomy multiplicity discipline Choosing the conditioning taxonomy among candidates to maximize coverage is selection problem; best held cell tables silently reintroduce it. Our discipline: (i) support-bin is pre-specified as the provenance thesis of this project, declared before the scale campaign ran; every headline table prints the pre-specified configuration, never per-cell winner; (ii) the support-bin-vs-pooled lift survives Bonferroni correction over the four candidate taxonomies (three comparisons at the Monte-Carlo floor: corrected < 1.5 104); (iii) an FWER-valid selection variant (LTT with δ/5 selection budget) picks the support family in 37/40 and 39/40 splits at α 0.15 but is underpowered at α=0.10, where it picks pooled in 29/40 splits we state this rather than oversell; (iv) the scale dump is superset of the 400-document dump on which support-bin was originally selected, so scale re-measurement is confirmation on overlapping data, not independent replication the independent check is the frozen-config run of 6.4.

sections.title: 6 Main results
sections.content: 6.1 The validity ladder on CORD Table 4 is the papers central result: four pre-specified operating points on the same 13,859 genuine claude-sonnet-5 fields, one per guarantee class. Read it with its annotations: the four rows bound different functionals under different assumptions, and the score differs across tiers (learned fusion at tier 1; shared 5-signal LR at tiers 24), so the column is menu of guarantee classes, not price curve for one score. Tier 1 (practical). The pre-specified recipe (learned fusion with all five signals, split-protocol add-one, pooled) attains coverage 0.318 at achieved risk 0.096 (SE 0.003 over the 40 resplits); the production variant that drops the NLI stage attains 0.326 at 0.097. This controls expected selective risk: it is an on-average operating point, not per-deployment certificate realized risk exceeded 0.10 in 47.5% (45% for the variant) of resplits, which is what mean-controlled bound sitting near its boundary looks like. No per-deployment or cross-corpus statement is licensed at this tier; reader who needs (violation) δ buys tier 3 at 0.318 0.171. Against the 5-signal LR control (pooled add-one, 0.134) the learned score is worth +0.184 coverage (p < 104); the split-protocol LR twin attains 0.128. Tier 2 (shared low-capacity fusion). The 5-signal LR with add-one support-bin reaches 0.212 at 0.095 under the split protocol. (The same cell with the LR refit on the threshold half is 0.218 at 0.096 statistically indistinguishable, consistent with the clean-fit control; we headline the split-protocol number.) Tier 3 (rigorous field-iid PAC, δ=0.10). Mondrian LTT with exact binomial tails certifies 0.171 coverage at achieved risk 0.068, violating in 1/40 splits and never returning an empty acceptance set. Label it precisely: PAC under field-iid idealization that is violated here (design effect 2) and empirically absorbed by the procedures conservatism (achieved risk 0.7α, violations δ); the cluster-corrected rung, which deflates the binomial evidence by the measured design effect, certifies 0.140 at 0.051 with zero violations the defensible field-level number, at cost of 0.031 coverage. Budget semantics: per-group rows make three separate δ=0.10 practical (learned 1. score) production variant 2. shared low-capacity fusion 3. PAC rigorous field-iid cluster-corrected Table 4: The validity ladder (CORD, 13,859 genuine claude-sonnet-5 fields, 800 docs, 49.0% correct; nominal α=0.10, δ=0.10 for PAC tiers; 40 document-level splits, seed 7; no tolerance band). Coverage is meansd; viol = fraction of splits with realized risk > α. Every grouped row beats its pooled counterpart at < 104 (sign-flip; in-corpus stability, 3.5). Vocabulary: tiers 12 control expected selective risk; only tiers 34 certify. tier procedure taxonomy (functional, coverage risk viol guarantee unit) E[sel. risk] α, field split add-one, HGB fusion, pooled 0.318 0.073 0.096 0.475 same E[sel. risk] α, field same, no-NLI score split add-one support-bin (LR) 0.326 0.046 0.212 0.030 0.097 0.095 0.45 0.35 (group risk > α) δ, field iid same, neff = n/deff LTT binom. mix, per-group support-bin LTT neff Holm, per-group support-bin LTT doc-Hoeffding, per-group support-bin 0.171 0.034 0.068 0.03 0.140 0.026 0.051 0. 0.060 0.058 0.020 0.00 4. rigorous doc-iid PAC (macro doc risk > α) δ, doc iid Tier 4 certifies nothing in 47.5% of splits; 0.020 is the zero-filled mean conditional on certifying anything, achieved risk is 0.038. Report both. statements; the simultaneous version certifies 0.160, still far above pooled at equal budget (0.091), so the support-bin lift is not budget artifact. Tier 4 (rigorous doc-iid PAC). The only assumption-honest certificate today, and we lead with its weakness rather than bury it: 0.060 mean coverage, certifying nothing in 19/40 splits (coverage 0.11 when it fires), risk 0.020 zero-filled / 0.038 conditional, and it bounds the macro per-document functional. This is the honest price of document-level exchangeability at 800 documents; powered doc-level procedures (clustered/variance-adaptive bounds) are the papers named open problem. The 0.060 already reflects the disclosed calibration-refit of 5.2; re-deriving it under fully frozen fit/val split (score fit on half the calibration documents, thresholds on the untouched other half) is markedly worse, 0.006 at α=0.10 the threshold-data halving costs an order of magnitude more coverage here than the refit leakage it removes (leakage alone is 0.006 coverage at every tier, confirming the 0 claim of 5.2 precisely). We report 0.060 as the tiers headline (consistent with tiers 13, which report the same disclosed-refit protocol) and 0.006 as the fully-rigorous floor. At α=0.05 the ladder compresses but survives: practical (production variant) 0.124 0.083 at 0.047 (viol 0.55); add-one support-bin 0.128 0.024 at 0.046 (viol 0.35; this cell is under the shared-calibration refit its split-protocol twin is 0.119 at 0.044); LTT mix per-group support-bin certifies 0.047 0.051 at 0.020 with zero violations. 6.2 Provenance wins every rigor tier on the sonnet CORD capture Table 5 crosses tiers with taxonomies on the corrected dump. With the shared fusion, support-bin the pre-specified provenance taxonomy is the best taxonomy at every tier: add-one 0.218 vs 0.144/0.134/0.127 for fieldtype-freq/pooled/fieldtype-rule; LTT 0.171 vs 0.097 (fieldtype-rule) and 0.0910.098 (pooled); doc-LTT 0.060 vs 0.006 for everything else (all lifts < 104, Bonferroni-corrected per 5.3). This is the first evidence that provenance certifiably pays at the rigorous tiers for selective risk control in document extraction; scoped, per 7, to the hard regime: on FUNSD and XFUND the ordering reverses. forensic footnote that strengthens the tie-mass diagnosis: on the defective no-NLI dump, fieldtype taxonomies won instead; restoring the continuous entailment signal (which un-ties the fused score) restores support-bin at every tier. The win is also model-scoped, not just corpus-scoped: re-running the full ladder on the same CORD documents under claude-haiku-4-5 and Qwen2.5-14B (weaker verbalized-confidence signal, AUROC 0.610/0.684 vs sonnets 0.845) collapses every PAC-tier cell to 0.005 coverage regardless of taxonomy, and the practical-tier money-table winners there are fieldtype-rule/-freq, not support-bin (sb-vs-pooled lifts p=0.121.0); PAC validity itself still transfers with zero violations. Support-bins advantage is established on the frontier-LLM (sonnet) capture; we do not claim it generalizes across extractors of differing signal quality. 7 Table 5: Taxonomy tier on CORD at α=0.10 (shared 5-signal fusion; coverage (risk) [viol]). Support-bin, pre-specified, wins every tier. On FUNSD (1,999 fields, 175 docs, 67.6% correct) the practical tier reaches 0.491 at 0.093, and rigorous certification is attainable but pooled LTT (0.280) beats every taxonomy, and the per-group fieldtype-rule certificate (0.128 at 0.034, zero violations) shows the machinery holds without taxonomy lift (lift not significant at this tier). To break that loop, the production configuration (learned no-NLI fusion, pooled split-protocol add-one; frozen before the run) was executed once, with no tuning, on selection-untouched genuine captures. On claude-haiku-4-5 CORD (5,341 fields, 400 docs, 56.7% correct) it attained coverage 0.167 at achieved risk 0.093 (viol 0.38) at α=0.10 and 0.068 at 0.037 at α=0.05 both held at nominal against near-zero 4-signal LR baseline (0.011). The transfer is non-trivial: haikus verbalized self-report is far weaker than sonnets (raw AUROC 0.610 vs 0.845; 0.621 vs 0.691 on matched fields about 70% of the raw gap is assertion-policy composition; haiku emits only 13 distinct confidence values (Gurram, 2026)), so the held result is evidence for the protocol, not for one models confidence quality. The same one-shot protocol on an open-weights capture Qwen2.5-14B served locally via vLLM, 6,168 CORD fields, 398 docs, 53.4% correct again held at both budgets: coverage 0.149 at achieved risk 0.099 (viol 0.47) at α=0.10 (no-NLI variant 0.138 at 0.088) and 0.048 at 0.036 at α=0.05, 6 gain over the 4-signal LR baseline (0.022). Across both untouched captures the risk contract never failed; what varies is coverage, which tracks the models signal quality (verbalized AUROC 0.845 / 0.684 / 0.610 for sonnet / qwen / haiku practical-tier coverage 0.326 / 0.149 / 0.167) dependence that broadly tracks signal quality (sonnet qwen haiku), consistent with the two-regime characterization (7), and the quantity the companion benchmark measures per model. Finally, the practical tiers guarantee was audited against human gold. Three independent annotators (blind, Fleiss κ = 0.83) re-judged 149 fields sampled from the production configurations accepted set at α=0.10: the human-verified selective risk is 2/149 = 1.3%, 95% CI [0.002, 0.048] an order of magnitude under budget. The audit also explains the margin: against human gold the automatic correctness labels used for calibration err one-sidedly pessimistic (21% of auto-flagged CORD errors are actually correct; 0% false-optimism), so thresholds fit against them 8 are conservative. The guarantee the ladder delivers is not only valid on untouched data; it is robust to the label noise it was computed under (Gurram, 2026).

sections.title: 7 When does conditioning pay? A two-regime characterization
sections.content: The campaigns ablations sharpen the old conditioning helps when provenance is discriminative intuition into two-regime empirical law. We state it with its mechanism and its scope, and formalize the laws idealized boundary cases in 7.1 (Assumption 1, Propositions 13); the general law away from that boundary remains pattern over three corpora and two score families, not proved rate. Regime 1: with learned score, covariates belong in the score. On the corrected CORD dump, every Mondrian taxonomy stacked on the learned fusion either violates nominal risk or loses coverage (pooled 0.318 held; support-bin 0.307 at 0.103, fieldtype-freq 0.272 at 0.101, fieldtype-rule 0.295 at 0.105 all violated). The controlled ablation (on the 4-signal scale run) makes it causal: field-type features are worth +0.069 coverage inside the score (p < 104); removing them and handing field-type to the taxonomy instead recovers essentially none of it (0.250 vs 0.326, 0.076, < 104); and fieldtype-Mondrian on top of the full score is actively harmful (0.062 freq / 0.036 rule, both < 104; corrected dump: 0.046, < 104 / 0.023, p=0.021). Mechanism: tree fusion splits on the covariate internally and equalizes per-group score scales, so external conditioning only fragments the threshold sample the per-group finite-sample penalty (which scales like plog(1/δ)/ng for the PAC tiers) buys nothing. Permutation importance confirms the score already consumes the signals (verbalized 0.130, support 0.068, consistencyverbalized 0.066). Regime 2: with weak or frozen score, covariates belong in the taxonomy where pooled cannot certify. For the shared LR the same conditioning is the single biggest lever: pooled 0.134 support-bin 0.218 (+0.084, < 104; split-protocol twins 0.128 0.212), and on the 4-signal run pooled 0.042 fieldtype 0.1330.135 (a 3 lift, < 104). At the rigorous tier the scoping is sharp: conditioning rescues certification where the pooled score head cannot certify at the target α (CORD, base correctness 0.490: support-bin 0.171 vs pooled 0.0910.098), and fragmentation costs coverage where pooled certifies fine (FUNSD, base correctness 0.676: pooled LTT 0.280 vs 0.149 for support-bin per-group; XFUND likewise favors pooled). The counterexample is printed, not hidden it is the boundary of the claim. Where the NLI signal lives. Entailment is droppable as feature of the learned score (no-NLI 0.326 full 0.318 on CORD, +0.008 difference within split noise, p=0.40; FUNSD differences not significant; on XFUND-de dropping it helps, +0.074 at α=0.05, p=0.0045) but is load-bearing for the shared fusion: it is the only fine-grained continuous signal, so it un-ties the score distribution that the threshold grid needs (backfilled: 34.4% nonzero entailment, 2,016 distinct fused values; the LRs add-one coverage on the corrected dump is 0.134 vs 0.037 with the dead column). sections.title: 8 The price of validity
sections.content: What does real certificate cost relative to the invalid folklore procedure? On the 6.9k CORD dump with support-bin conditioning  (Table 8)  , the per-group PAC certificate retains 28% of the invalid add-one coverage at α=0.10, 42% at 0.15, and 84% at 0.20 and 0% at 0.05, where 200 calibration documents simply cannot support 90%-confidence certificate. Rigor is knob: the certificates cost collapses as the risk budget grows, which is exactly the operating guidance practitioner needs. sections.title: 9 Limitations
sections.content: One corpus certifies non-trivially. The full rigorous ladder certifies useful coverage on CORDsonnet only; FUNSD certifies 0.128 rigorously but its taxonomy lift is not significant, and XFUND-de is small-n. The frozen-config haiku confirmation (6.4) is the first out-of-selection replication; full ladders on haiku and an open-weights extractor are queued. The doc-iid tier is honest but near-vacuous (0.060 coverage, 47.5% zero-coverage splits). Powered document-level PAC procedures are the named open problem. The theorem covers idealized boundary cases, not the general regime. 7.1 proves the conditioning-dominates and subsumption directions at the ρ = 0 boundary (Assumption 1) and states that results degrade linearly in ρ, but does not prove quantitative rate for ρ > 0; the finite-sample penalty (Proposition 2) is worst-case Hoeffding/union bound, not tight one. The sign prediction is verified on all three corpora (7.4), still n=3. Inference is in-corpus. All 40 resplits share documents; sign-flip p-values are split-stability statements with Monte-Carlo floor of 104, and the scale dump overlaps the dump on which support-bin was first selected (5.3). Score refit on calibration at tiers 24 is disclosed in 5.2; the measured effect is 0 for the 5-parameter LR, and the harness adopts fit-half freezing as hygiene. Label quality. FUNSD free-text correctness is protocol-dependent (automatic-protocol agreement κ=0.10 vs 0.78 for structured CORD fields; Appendix C); certificate against noisy labels is certificate about those labels. The companions human-gold audit bounds the practical impact: automatic labels err one-sidedly pessimistic, and the human-verified 11 accepted-set risk is 1.3% against the 10% budget (6.4); scaling human gold to FUNSD/XFUND is future work.

sections.title: 10 Release
sections.content: VerifyDoc is released Apache-2.0: pip-installable library, CLI, review UI, an MCP server, and the evaluation harness that regenerates every number in this paper from configuration (fixed seeds, pinned splits, chained bit-exact sanity gates, and the 463/624-cells regression check of Appendix B). The library also ships trust-gated agentic layer (repair / adjudicate / adaptive-k) that routes review fields through escalation tiers; we release it as an artifact and leave its empirical evaluation to future work the companion ensemble study (Gurram, 2026) shows naive multi-extractor adjudication inherits dominant models hallucinations, so the gate, not the ensemble, carries the trust contract.

sections.title: A Guarantee statements and procedure details
sections.content: Tiers 12 (add-one, marginal). With calibration and test fields exchangeable, the add-one threshold of 4 controls E[selective risk] α over calibration/test draws (Geifman & El-Yaniv, 2019; Preprint authors, 2025b); the field is the exchangeability unit; no per-draw statement is made. Document clustering violates exchangeability at the document level; the split protocol removes scorethreshold dependence only. Tier 3 (Mondrian LTT). For group g, candidate t, let nt be accepted calibration fields and kt the errors among them. The exact binomial tail pt = Pr[Bin(nt, α) kt] tests H0 : Rg(t) > α. Reject over the 15-candidate grid with δ/2 Holm step-down plus δ/2 fixed-sequence (most conservative first, stop at first non-rejection); by the union bound the pair is FWER-valid at δ; the chosen threshold is the certified candidate with the largest calibration acceptance. Per-group budgets give each group its own δ (three statements); the simultaneous form spends δ/G. Exact binomial dominates Hoeffding-style tails for binary losses (measured: 0.022 exact-binomial vs 0.013 Hoeffding coverage on the 6.9k dump). Pure fixed-sequence with many groups can silently fail (lucky-zero tiny-n bins: the groundedsupport taxonomy violated on mean, risk 0.103, 25% of splits); the mix rule is the variant that never collapsed across corpora. Cluster correction. ltt.neff replaces nt by nt/ddeff with the plug-in design effect estimated from per-document error clustering approximate (the deff is estimated), and uniformly more conservative. Tier 4 (doc-iid). Per accepting document d, the loss is its within-document error rate among accepted fields; finite-sample Hoeffding bound over documents tests whether the mean per-document loss exceeds α, with the same Holm/fixed-sequence machinery. Documents iid; bounds the macro functional. Full disclosure: the entailment-capture defect and its forensics The first 13,859-field CORD capture shipped entailment 0.0 for all fields: mid-capture torch swap made the NLI stage skip silently (logged per field as entailment skipped, with torch-compile indexing error). The defect surfaced as two anomalies: rigorous certified coverage shrank 4 when the data doubled, and the doc-level add-one returned exactly 0. Root cause: with the only fine-grained continuous signal dead, the fused score collapsed to 257 distinct values (tie masses of 221/183 fields at the acceptance head), so the smallest realizable candidate accepted 245 fields at empirical risk 0.114 uncertifiable at any confidence. Counterfactual reproduction: zeroing entailment on the intact 6.9k dump reproduces the collapse (0.0302 0.0011 certified coverage; 0.0371 0.0000 doc add-one). Hardening: candidate thresholds are snapped to the nearest distinct-value boundary (ties toward the smaller, more conservative count; label-independent); regression gate re-runs the full pre-fix grid 463/624 cells bit-identical, maximum headline-alpha drift 0.0088 ( 0.16 of one split-sd) and grid-only ablation shows the fix moves certified coverage by at most 0.004: the binding pathology was the degenerate score, not the grid. After the NLI backfill (34.4% nonzero entailment, 2,016 distinct fused values) both grids were re-run to produce this papers numbers. Diagnostic lesson: the tail looks cleaner at scale was stable-argsort illusion under ties; the threshold-realizable top-1% error was 0.071 (vs 0.045 intact).
